summary: ptracemusl's delayed and delayed-poll rows and its entry row on x86-64, each booted alone, on a kernel built from a private copy with the debug-entry fixture of tests/proofs/ptrace_fixture.py, with faults in the forced delivery of a deferred hit, in signal_pending's view of it, and in the fixture itself; the entry row and the faults of the debug interrupt stack and GS are this architecture's alone

argv: ARCH=x86_64 exec sh tests/proofs/ptrace.sh rows ${WORK} delayed delayed-poll entry

faults.name: unforced
faults.summary: a deferred user hit posted to the thread in place of forced, so that the blocked SIGTRAP waits

lines: delayed debug exception lost its frame or result

faults.name: pending
faults.summary: signal_pending ignores the pending debug status, so that an infinite poll sleeps on

lines: delayed infinite poll did not trap

faults.name: missing-injection
faults.summary: the fixture without its int $1 at the system-call entry, so that no debug exception is taken there

lines: delayed debug exception lost its status

faults.name: wrong-entry-pc
faults.summary: the fixture without its entry PC, so that debugreg_defer_user does not take the PC after int $1 for the entry's

lines: delayed debug exception lost its status

faults.name: stack
faults.summary: the debug exception's gate given no interrupt stack, so that a hit on an invalid user stack double faults

faults.name: gs
faults.summary: the debug entry chooses GS by the saved CS, which is still the user's at the system-call entry, so that the machine resets
